title: ACME POC timeline and milestones
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline for ACME's inference pilot. Redwood AE + SE walked through milestone plan (kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout). Key constraints: data residency, latency p95 target, throughput, cost objectives, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send SOW, benchmark plan, and access checklist; ACME to provision sample dataset and staging infra credentials.
next_steps: Jordan to send draft POC SOW and pricing by 2025-12-10
Priya to share benchmark harness and sample inference script by 2025-12-12
Aisha to provide S3 access and staging VPC details by 2025-12-11
action_items: Jordan Mills - send SOW & POC timeline - due 2025-12-10
Priya Nair - share benchmark harness + runbook - due 2025-12-12
Aisha Khan - provide sample dataset access (S3) + staging IPs - due 2025-12-11
Sam Peterson - provide representative workload profile (qps/seq length) - due 2025-12-12
transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-08 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Peterson (ACME Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Infra), Liu Wei (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey team, thanks for joining - Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick intros, then we'll go through the POC milestones and confirm success criteria.
[00:15] Sam: Hi Jordan, Sam here, head of ML at ACME. We're looking to validate inference for a rerank + convo assistant workload, mainly concerned about latency and cost.
[00:30] Aisha: Aisha, infra. We'll own provisioning and security checks.
[00:35] Priya: Priya, SE at Redwood. I'll run the benchmarks and help with the integration.
[00:45] Liu: Liu, CTO - short on time but want to make sure exec readout line up.

[01:05] Jordan: Great. High level: we propose a 6-week pilot, four milestones - kickoff, access & baseline setup, mid-point review with initial benchmarks, and an exec readout. The goal is to validate p95 latency, throughput, and cost per 1k reqs so you can decide on Dedicated vs Hosted or Private deployment.
[01:25] Sam: That sounds right. Can you be specific on success criteria? We're aiming for p95 <100ms for short prompts and sustain about 50 rps for our batch rerank at peak. Cost target is ~30% below our current in-house infra.
[01:45] Priya: Okay noted. For the POC we'll define explicit pass/fail thresholds: p95 latency <100ms for 512-token context on the chat path, sustained 50 rps for the reranker with tail latency under 200ms, and a cost delta calculation from the benchmark. We'll also track quality - no regression vs your baseline.
[02:10] Aisha: On security, we need SOC2 docs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integrations; if we go Private we'll need VPC peering or on-prem options.
[02:25] Jordan: We have an enterprise security pack - SOC2 + audits are included; we can provide SAML SSO and KMS integration notes. We'll attach the security whitepaper. For Private, there's an add-on for VPC/on-prem installs.

[03:00] Sam: What's the workload sizing you need from us? We can share QPS, typical seq length distribution, and sample payloads.
[03:10] Priya: Perfect - we'll need: peak qps, 95/99 percentiles of sequence lengths, tokenization samples, and a sample dataset ~10k records for quality checks. Also, do you have a baseline model and current infra numbers (latency/cost per token)?
[03:30] Sam: We have baseline numbers - I'll export them. Currently ~150ms p95 for our hosted provider and cost is X per 1k tokens. We'll send a spreadsheet.

[04:00] Liu: Timeline: how quickly can we get meaningful results? We prefer a mid-point at week 3 with initial benchmarks to show to engineering leadership.
[04:10] Jordan: That's our recommendation - kickoff week 0, access + environment prep in week 1, run baseline and initial benchmarks week 2-3, mid-point review at end of week 3, then tuning and final exec readout end of week 6.
[04:30] Priya: On the benchmarks: we'll run two flows - interactive chat and batch rerank. For chat we measure p50/p95/p99 for 64-312 tokens; for rerank we'll measure throughput and distribution of latencies across varying batch sizes. We'll supply the harness and expected commands.

[05:05] Aisha: About data movement: can you support bringing inference to our VPC? We prefer not to send PII out.
[05:15] Jordan: Yes - Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and on-premized options. For the POC, you can either share deidentified sample data in S3 or we can run in your VPC if you prefer.
[05:30] Sam: We'll try to provide deidentified samples first to speed the process. If the mid-point shows we need private, we'll heat up the VPC option.

[06:00] Priya: A couple of practical items: we recommend starting with a mid-sized open model we know performs well on our runtime for a fair baseline (we'll suggest a specific model and quantization profile). Also, we'll capture KV cache and batching behavior because that affects tail latency.
[06:25] Sam: Good - do you have vendor lock-in concerns? We've been considering Vertex and OpenAI.
[06:35] Jordan: We often hear that. For ACME the differentiator is predictable economics and the ability to run the same stack across Hosted/Dedicated/Private which avoids lock-in to a single cloud provider. We also provide rollout policies and fallback model variants to keep uptime.

[07:10] Liu: Pricing and SOW - what do we expect to see? We need a clear statement of work for executive sign-off.
[07:20] Jordan: We'll send a draft POC SOW with milestones, acceptance criteria, and optional pricing for Dedicated/Private. Expect that by Wednesday (2025-12-10).

[08:00] Sam: For benchmarks, what tooling will you use and how do we validate results?
[08:10] Priya: We'll share a benchmark harness (python scripts + metrics) and a reproducibility doc. We'll also save full traces for a 1:1 review. You can run the harness from your staging VPC or we can run it from Redwood if credentials are shared. Either way, results will be compared to your baseline spreadsheet.

[09:00] Aisha: Ok. SSO/SAML mapping and RBAC are required. We'll need role mappings for dev/test and exec reviewers.
[09:12] Jordan: Noted - we'll include RBAC config examples.

[10:00] Sam: Any blockers on our side? We'll need an expected checklist.
[10:08] Priya: Checklist: S3 sample data URL (deidentified), staging VPC CIDRs if you want the runner in your cloud, service account for the benchmark harness OR a temporary Redwood-run option, and the baseline metrics spreadsheet. Once we have those we can start environment setup in under 48 hours.

[11:00] Liu: Sounds good. Quick note: exec readout should include cost delta analysis and risk assessment.
[11:10] Jordan: We'll prepare a short exec slide deck for the readout.

[11:45] Sam: Timing recap?
[11:50] Jordan: Kickoff week of 2025-12-15, access & baseline setup by 2025-12-19, initial benchmarks weeks 2-3, mid-point review end of week 3 (approx 2025-12-29), final tuning weeks 4-6, exec readout by 2026-01-23.
[12:10] Aisha: Can we move mid-point earlier? We prefer an interim checkpoint in week 2 as well, maybe a short tech sync.
[12:18] Priya: We can do a short tech sync at week 2 and then the formal mid-point at week 3.

[13:00] Jordan: To recap action items - I'll send SOW and timeline, Priya will send the harness and runbook, Aisha to provide sample data and staging access, Sam to send baseline numbers. We'll aim to kick off the week of Dec 15.
[13:20] Sam: Thanks - that works.
[13:30] Liu: Thanks everyone, we'll review the SOW and come back with questions.
[13:40] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments (SOW, security docs, benchmark harness link, checklist).

[14:00] End of call.
